chunks: He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurariy informed me, saying: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Zurariy narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, blessings of Allah be upon them both, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said:
Whenever the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, stood to deliver a sermon, he would praise Allah and extol Him. Then he would say:

'Now then, indeed the most truthful speech is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, and the worst of affairs are their innovations, and every innovation is misguidance.'

He would raise his voice, and his cheeks would turn red, and he would remind people of the Hour and its coming, as though he were warning of an advancing army, saying: 'The Hour has come upon you in the morning, the Hour has come upon you in the evening!'

Then he would say: 'I was sent together with the Hour like these two' — and he would join his two forefingers — 'Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his family, and whoever leaves behind a debt, it is my responsibility and mine to bear.'

key_terms.السَّاعَة: The Hour; the Day of Judgment and Resurrection, a central eschatological concept in Islam.
key_terms.بِدْعَة: Religious innovation; introducing new practices into worship that have no basis in the Quran or Sunnah, considered a form of misguidance.
key_terms.خُطْبَة: Formal sermon or address, typically delivered before the Friday congregational prayer or on Islamic holidays.
key_terms.هُدَى: Guidance; divine direction toward the straight path, particularly as embodied in the Prophet’s practice.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say in his standard sermon about the Quran, innovation, and the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain of narrators from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) from his forefathers, describes the standard sermon (khutba) practice of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Delivered in Medina to the early Muslim community, the sermon follows a formulaic pattern that became the template for all subsequent Friday and Eid sermons in Islamic tradition. The Prophet would begin with praise of Allah, then declare the absolute primacy of the Quran as the truest speech and his own Sunnah as the best guidance, while warning sternly against religious innovation (bid’a). His passionate delivery — raising his voice, cheeks turning red — conveyed the urgency of his eschatological message: the Day of Judgment is imminent. His gesture of joining two fingers illustrates how close his prophetic mission is to the Final Hour. The sermon closes with a remarkable social pledge: the Prophet personally assumes responsibility for the debts of deceased Muslims, while their estates go to their families. This combined spiritual-temporal authority reflects his unique status as both religious guide and communal guardian.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 1. He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurariy who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzar, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon both of them, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:
Whenever the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny stood to address, he would praise Allah and thank Him. Then he would say:

"Know you all, that the most veracious and truthful statement is the Book of Allah (i.e. the Qu’ran) and the best guidance is that of Muhammad. The worst things are those which are invented concoctions, and every such innovation is misleading."

Then he would raise his voice, with his cheeks gradually turning red and remind people of the Day of Reckoning and its dawn, in the manner one warns of an advancing army of the enemy. He would say: "It dawns with you every morning and is with you every evening!"

Then he would say: "I have been sent to you with the Day of Reckoning like these two (then he would join his two forefingers). Whoever leaves behind him wealth, that will go to its heirs and whoever leaves behind a debt, it is my responsibility."
